entities.name: Sandworm
entities.gloss: A Russian state-sponsored cyber espionage and sabotage group also tracked as APT44 and UAC-0002.

entities.name: UAC-0133
entities.gloss: A threat group and suspected subcluster of Sandworm (UAC-0002) targeting critical infrastructure.

entities.name: QUEUESEED
entities.gloss: A C++ backdoor malware family also tracked as KNUCKLETOUCH, ICYWELL, WRONGSENS, and KAPEKA.

entities.name: LOADGRIP
entities.gloss: A C-based ELF injector malware used to decrypt and inject payloads on Linux systems via ptrace API.

entities.name: BIASBOAT
entities.gloss: A C-based Linux variant of the QUEUESEED backdoor malware distributed as an encrypted ELF payload.

entities.name: WEEVELY
entities.gloss: A stealthy PHP webshell designed for remote server administration and command execution.

entities.name: REGEORG.NEO
entities.gloss: A web-based tunneling tool used to establish SOCKS proxies through web servers via HTTP/HTTPS.

entities.name: PIVOTNACCI
entities.gloss: A PHP-based tunneling and proxy tool used for lateral movement in compromised networks.

entities.name: GOSSIPFLOW
entities.gloss: A Go-based malware providing tunneling and SOCKS5 proxy functionality using the Yamux multiplexer library.

entities.name: SDELETE
entities.gloss: A secure file deletion command-line utility from Microsoft Sysinternals used in destructive cyber attacks.

entities.name: CHISEL
entities.gloss: A fast TCP/UDP tunnel tool written in Go and transported over HTTP/WebSockets.

entities.name: LIBPROCESSHIDER
entities.gloss: A Linux library used to hide processes under Linux using the LD_PRELOAD hooking technique.

entities.name: JUICYPOTATONG
entities.gloss: A Windows privilege escalation tool derived from JuicyPotato for abusing SeImpersonatePrivilege.

entities.name: ROTTENPOTATONG
entities.gloss: A Windows local privilege escalation tool designed to abuse token impersonation privileges.

entities.name: Україна
entities.gloss: A country in Eastern Europe whose critical infrastructure was targeted by Sandworm.
